package_info.package_versions: all published versions (over 17,000 packages, all versions affected)
package_info.why_malicious: The packages are intentionally crafted with enticing names and descriptions to attract users, then direct them to phishing sites via README.md and package descriptions. This is part of a coordinated spam campaign to distribute phishing links, harvest credentials, and generate profit through referral rewards. The presence of automation scripts and helper files in the packages further confirms the malicious intent and large-scale automation of the attack.

execution_context.trigger: import-time (when viewing package details or README)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the README.md displays a phishing link, enticing users to click, which initiates a browser request to an external phishing website, potentially leading to credential theft or further redirection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: README.md files containing links to unrelated, suspicious domains that promise free resources are a well-known phishing tactic designed to lure users into visiting malicious sites.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages use README.md for documentation relevant to the project, not for promoting external phishing campaigns or unrelated offers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may link to official project homepages or documentation, but never to unrelated 'free' offers or suspicious third-party domains.
key_indicators: README.md contains links to non-project, non-documentation domains
Enticing language promising free followers, cheats, or resources
Links point to known phishing or scam domains

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
for folder in config_folders:
    with open(os.path.join(folder, 'config.txt')) as f:
        domain, keyword = f.read().splitlines()
    title = generate_random_title(keyword)
    description = generate_random_description(keyword)
    link = f'https://{domain}/{random.randint(1000,9999)}'
    with open('README.md', 'w') as readme:
        readme.write(f'[Click here for {title}]({link})')
    os.system('npm publish')
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package publication, the automation script reads configuration files, generates random phishing links and enticing titles, writes these into README.md, and publishes the package to npm, resulting in mass distribution of phishing packages with unique links.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated generation and publication of thousands of packages with randomized phishing links and titles is a clear indicator of a malicious, large-scale phishing campaign.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package publication is manual or semi-automated for legitimate projects, not for mass-producing spam or phishing packages with randomized content.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automation scripts are used in CI/CD for legitimate package publication, but not for generating and distributing mass phishing campaigns.
key_indicators: Script generates random links and titles for each package
Script writes phishing links to README.md files
Script publishes large numbers of packages in a loop
Presence of helper files and automation scripts in package tarballs

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After successful publication, the script appends the URL of the published package to a local log file, enabling tracking and management of all distributed phishing packages.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Tracking published phishing packages is a tactic used in coordinated campaigns to monitor reach, manage updates, and facilitate further propagation of malicious links.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: While normal scripts may log published package URLs for auditing, doing so as part of a mass phishing operation is a clear deviation from standard practice.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: CI/CD systems may log published artifacts for legitimate auditing and traceability.
key_indicators: Logging of mass-published package URLs to a local file
Integration with phishing link generation and publication automation

driver.get('https://news-site.com/wp-login.php')
driver.find_element(By.ID, 'user_login').send_keys(username)
driver.find_element(By.ID, 'user_pass').send_keys(password)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After package publication, the automation script uses Selenium to log into WordPress sites with stored credentials, creates new posts containing links to the published npm package, and publishes them, amplifying the phishing campaign by propagating links on unrelated external websites.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated posting of package links to unrelated news or blog sites using browser automation and credentials is a strong indicator of coordinated malicious promotion and spam propagation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate package publication does not involve spamming unrelated websites with package links, especially via automated browser scripts and credentialed logins.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated blog posting is legitimate for content syndication or marketing, but not for propagating phishing or spam campaigns.
key_indicators: Use of Selenium or browser automation for posting
Hardcoded or stored credentials in automation scripts
Posting package links to unrelated news or blog sites

behavioral_signatures: README.md or package description contains links to unrelated, suspicious domains, especially those promising free resources or cheats
Mass publication of packages with similar names and descriptions in a short time frame
Presence of automation scripts (e.g., publish_script.py) or helper files in package tarballs that generate and publish packages
Automated posting of package links to unrelated external websites using browser automation
file_indicators: README.md with phishing or referral links to non-project domains
helper.txt or automation scripts (e.g., publish_script.py) present in package tarballs
index.js and package.json files generated from templates with random or generic content
network_indicators: Outbound links to known phishing domains (e.g., betapps.club, stumblegems.site, followersfree.store, etc.) in README.md or descriptions
Automated traffic to npm publish endpoints from the same source in rapid succession
Automated logins and posts to WordPress or news-like sites using browser automation
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages whose README.md or descriptions contain links to non-project, non-documentation domains, especially those promising free resources or cheats. Flag packages published in large batches with similar naming patterns or randomized content. Inspect package tarballs for automation scripts or helper files unrelated to the package's stated functionality. Track automated posting of package links to unrelated external sites using browser automation. Correlate with known phishing domains and referral URLs to identify coordinated campaigns.
